provenance.source: NCERT Mathematics Class 8, Chapter 1 'Rational Numbers' — additive inverse. The four misconceptions are the ones this topic reliably produces: reciprocal confusion, the belief that an inverse must be negative, treating the three ways of writing a negative fraction as different numbers, and denying zero an inverse.
provenance.note: m1 (additive vs multiplicative inverse) is the one that matters. It is the single most common error on this topic and it is a genuine concept gap, not a slip — a student holding it will also get 'role of one' wrong later, which is why c8-math-ch1-t3 lists this topic as a prerequisite. concepts.title: Additive inverse
concepts.statement: The additive inverse of a rational number $\frac{a}{b}$ is the number which, when added to it, gives 0. That is, $\frac{a}{b} + \left(-\frac{a}{b}\right) = 0$. It is also called the ‘negative’ of that number.
concepts.hook: Think you have ₹50 and you have borrowed ₹50 from a friend. What is the total? Zero. This ₹50 and -₹50 cancel each other — this is the additive inverse. Now the question: if you have -₹50, meaning a debt of ₹50, what do you need to make it zero?

analogies.text: Going 3 floors up in a lift and then coming 3 floors down — back to the same place.
In cricket, you scored 4 runs and then got a penalty of 4 runs — net zero.
The temperature rose by 5° and then fell by 5° — back to the same temperature.

formulas.note: b ≠ 0. This is the definition of additive inverse.
All three are the same number, only the way of writing is different.
This is the multiplicative inverse — different from additive. Multiplying by this gives 1, not adding.

misconceptions.wrong_belief: Additive inverse means turn it upside down — the inverse of $\frac{3}{5}$ is $\frac{5}{3}$.
misconceptions.why_wrong: That is the multiplicative inverse (reciprocal), which gives 1 when multiplied. The additive inverse gives 0 when added. Check and see: $\frac{3}{5} + \frac{5}{3}$ does not give 0.
misconceptions.correction: If you have to add, change the sign. If you have to multiply, turn it upside down.
misconceptions.probe: What should I add to $\frac{3}{5}$ to get 0? And what should I multiply by to get 1? These are two different questions.

misconceptions.wrong_belief: The additive inverse is always negative.
misconceptions.why_wrong: If the number itself is negative, its inverse will be positive — because to make 0, you need the opposite sign, not a negative sign.
misconceptions.correction: The additive inverse of $-\frac{11}{4}$ is $+\frac{11}{4}$. The sign becomes OPPOSITE, not always negative.
misconceptions.probe: What will you add to $-\frac{11}{4}$ to get 0? Will it be positive or negative?

misconceptions.why_wrong: All three have the same value, only the way of writing is different. On the number line, all three sit at the same place.
misconceptions.correction: Whether the sign is in the numerator, in the denominator, or in front of the whole fraction — the value does not change.
misconceptions.probe: Write $\frac{3}{-5}$ in standard form. Now tell me, is it different from $\frac{-3}{5}$ or the same?

misconceptions.wrong_belief: 0 does not have an additive inverse.
misconceptions.why_wrong: $0 + 0 = 0$, so 0 is its own additive inverse. The definition says ‘the number which, when added, gives 0’ — 0 satisfies this condition.
misconceptions.correction: 0 is the only number which is its own additive inverse.
misconceptions.probe: What should we add to 0 to get 0? Can it be 0 itself?

worked_examples.problem: Find the additive inverse of $\frac{7}{9}$ and verify it.
steps: Additive inverse means change the sign: $-\frac{7}{9}$
The number is already negative, so its inverse will be positive

worked_examples.problem: Find both the additive inverse and the multiplicative inverse of $\frac{5}{8}$, and show the difference.
steps: Additive inverse: change the sign → $-\frac{5}{8}$. Check: $\frac{5}{8} + \left(-\frac{5}{8}\right) = 0$ ✓
Multiplicative inverse: turn it upside down → $\frac{8}{5}$. Check: $\frac{5}{8} \times \frac{8}{5} = 1$ ✓
Difference: one gives 0 when added, the other gives 1 when multiplied

questions.stem: What is the additive inverse of $\frac{5}{8}$?
questions.solution: Change the sign: $-\frac{5}{8}$. Check: $\frac{5}{8} + \left(-\frac{5}{8}\right) = 0$. $\frac{8}{5}$ is the multiplicative inverse — multiplying by it gives 1, not 0 when added.

questions.stem: What is the additive inverse of $\frac{-13}{7}$?
questions.solution: The number is already negative, so its inverse will be positive: $\frac{13}{7}$. Check: $\frac{-13}{7} + \frac{13}{7} = 0$.

questions.stem: If $x$ is the additive inverse of $\frac{-4}{9}$, what is the value of $x + \frac{2}{9}$? (to two decimal places)
questions.solution: The additive inverse of $\frac{-4}{9}$ is $x = \frac{4}{9}$. So $\frac{4}{9} + \frac{2}{9} = \frac{6}{9} = \frac{2}{3} \approx 0.667$.

questions.stem: Prove that the additive inverse is unique in rational numbers — that is, one number cannot have two different additive inverses.

rubric: Maan liya ki $a$ ke do additive inverse hain, $y$ aur $z$
$y = y + 0 = y + (a + z) = (y + a) + z$ — associativity ka istemaal
$= 0 + z = z$, isliye $y = z$ aur inverse unique hai

questions.solution: Suppose $a$ has two additive inverses: $y$ and $z$. Then $a + y = 0$ and $a + z = 0$. Now $y = y + 0 = y + (a + z) = (y + a) + z = 0 + z = z$. Here, both zero being the additive identity and addition being associative have been used. Since $y = z$, the additive inverse is unique.

questions.stem: What is the additive inverse of $0$?

options.text: $0$ has no additive inverse at all

questions.solution: $0 + 0 = 0$, so 0 is its own additive inverse. This is the only number for which this happens.

questions.stem: Which of these is NOT equal to $\frac{-3}{5}$?
questions.solution: $\frac{3}{-5}$, $-\left(\frac{3}{5}\right)$ and $\frac{-6}{10}$ — all three have the value $\frac{-3}{5}$. Only $\frac{3}{5}$ is different; it is the additive inverse of $\frac{-3}{5}$.

questions.stem: By which number should $\frac{5}{8}$ be multiplied to get $1$?
questions.solution: $\frac{5}{8} \times \frac{8}{5} = 1$ — this is the multiplicative inverse. $-\frac{5}{8}$ is the additive inverse; adding it gives 0, not multiplying. This question has been asked the other way round on purpose, so that the difference between the two becomes clear.

questions.stem: Neha wrote: ‘The additive inverse of $\frac{2}{7}$ is $\frac{7}{2}$ because both together cancel the number.’ What is her mistake?

options.text: $\frac{7}{2}$ is the multiplicative inverse — the value of $\frac{2}{7} + \frac{7}{2}$ does not come out as 0
There is no mistake, $\frac{7}{2}$ is correct
The mistake is only in the sign; the answer should be $-\frac{7}{2}$
$\frac{2}{7}$ has no additive inverse at all

questions.solution: ‘Cancel’ happens in two ways, and both are different. The one that gives 0 when added is the additive inverse — $-\frac{2}{7}$. The one that gives 1 when multiplied is the multiplicative inverse — $\frac{7}{2}$. Neha wrote the second one in place of the first one.

questions.stem: The additive inverse of $\frac{-7}{12}$ is $\frac{p}{12}$. What will be the value of $p$?
questions.solution: The additive inverse of $\frac{-7}{12}$ is $\frac{7}{12}$, because $\frac{-7}{12} + \frac{7}{12} = 0$. So $p = 7$.

questions.stem: $a = \frac{-5}{6}$ is given. Add the additive inverse of $a$ and the multiplicative inverse of $a$. Write the answer to four decimal places.
questions.solution: Additive inverse: $\frac{5}{6}$. Multiplicative inverse: $\frac{-6}{5}$ (because $\frac{-5}{6} \times \frac{-6}{5} = 1$). Add: $\frac{5}{6} + \frac{-6}{5} = \frac{25}{30} - \frac{36}{30} = \frac{-11}{30} \approx -0.3667$. Notice — the multiplicative inverse of a negative number is also negative.

questions.stem: Explain to a friend the difference between additive inverse and multiplicative inverse. Give one example of both.

rubric: Additive inverse: jodne par 0 deta hai, sign badalkar milta hai
Multiplicative inverse: guna karne par 1 deta hai, ulta karke milta hai
Ek number pe dono dikhaye, jaise $\frac{3}{4}$ ka $-\frac{3}{4}$ aur $\frac{4}{3}$

questions.solution: Additive inverse is the number which, when added, gives 0 — change the sign. The additive inverse of $\frac{3}{4}$ is $-\frac{3}{4}$, because $\frac{3}{4} + \left(-\frac{3}{4}\right) = 0$. Multiplicative inverse is the number which, when multiplied, gives 1 — turn it upside down. The multiplicative inverse of $\frac{3}{4}$ is $\frac{4}{3}$, because $\frac{3}{4} \times \frac{4}{3} = 1$. Way to remember: if you have to ADD, change the SIGN; if you have to MULTIPLY, turn it UPSIDE DOWN.
